newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine must debut foreign bond in early 97 - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine must debut foreign bond in early 97 - c.bank.

text.p: Ukraine must issue its first foreign-currency bonds in the first quarter of 1997 to cover the projected budget deficit, the central bank chief said.
Viktor Yushchenko said the bank would tender its project to release the bonds to foreign firms. The first issue would be for about $50 million.

"The central bank's position is that Ukraine can get away without printing money next year to cover the deficit and can cover it with local securities and foreign bonds," Viktor Yushchenko told reporters.
The deficit in the 1997 draft budget is 4.09 billion hryvnia ($2.15 billion), four percent of gross domestic product using Ukrainian methods, or 2.4 percent by Western standards.
The draft says internal sources would pay for 200 billion hryvnia of the gap and foreign credits would cover 209 billion.
Yushchenko said Ukraine could win a similar credit rating to other former Soviet republics like Russia and Kazakhstan. The country has not yet received an international rating.
